name: Databricks
description: Databricks is a cloud-based data intelligence platform built on the lakehouse architecture, unifying data engineering, data warehousing, and AI/ML workloads on open formats like Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, with governance through Unity Catalog and natural-language analytics via Genie.
best_for: Data engineering, data science, and analytics teams that want a single lakehouse platform spanning ETL, SQL analytics, and AI/ML model development across AWS, Azure, and GCP, rather than stitching together separate warehouse and data-science tools.
features: Lakehouse architecture built on Delta Lake (ACID transactions, time travel) with native Apache Iceberg support for open table formats
Lakeflow for unified data ingestion and pipeline orchestration across batch and streaming sources
Serverless SQL analytics for BI and reporting on the same copy of data used for engineering and ML
Unity Catalog for centralized governance, permissions, lineage, and auditing across data and AI assets
Genie, a natural-language interface for asking business questions and generating insights grounded in an organization's own data
Agent Bricks framework for building and orchestrating custom AI agents with third-party or open models
Databricks Apps for deploying data and AI applications directly on the platform
Lakebase, a Postgres-based operational database for combining transactional and analytical workloads
pros: Runs natively on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, so teams aren't locked into one cloud provider
Built on open formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg) and open-source Apache Spark, reducing proprietary lock-in
Databricks Free Edition offers a genuinely no-cost way to learn the platform, separate from the time-limited trial
cons: Consumption-based DBU pricing makes month-to-month costs harder to predict than a flat per-seat fee
No published self-serve price list for compute rates — teams must use the pricing calculator or talk to sales to estimate real-world cost

pricing.starting_price: Usage-based, billed per Databricks Unit (DBU); no flat starting price is published

tiers.name: Free Edition
tiers.notes: Perpetually free workspace for learning, prototyping, and experimentation (replaced the retired Community Edition on January 1, 2026); no guaranteed reliability, support, or SLA.

tiers.name: Pay-as-you-go
tiers.notes: Consumption-based billing per Databricks Unit (DBU), metered per second of compute. Exact per-DBU rate depends on cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP), region, and workload type. Committed-use discounts are available for larger usage commitments.

alternatives.name: Snowflake
alternatives.description: A cross-cloud data platform for storage, compute, and increasingly AI/ML workloads, also billed on a consumption basis.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want a warehouse-first cloud data platform with simple credit-based consumption pricing and strong third-party data sharing/marketplace features.
strengths: Cortex AI for in-platform LLM access

faq.question: Is Databricks free to use?
faq.answer: Databricks offers a perpetually free Free Edition for learning, prototyping, and experimentation (which replaced the retired Community Edition on January 1, 2026), plus a 14-day free trial of the full platform for evaluating production workloads.

faq.question: How is Databricks priced?
faq.answer: Databricks bills on a consumption basis using Databricks Units (DBUs), a normalized measure of compute metered per second, rather than a flat per-seat or per-plan price. Exact per-DBU rates vary by cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP), region, and workload type, and committed-use discounts are available for larger commitments.

faq.question: Which clouds does Databricks run on?
faq.answer: Databricks is available natively on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
